title: Cache invalidation and the problem of stale data

videos.script: The owner of the bookshop lowers a price. The database has the new price at once. {{update}} The visitors keep seeing the old one. Nothing is broken. The cache was told the answer was good for a minute, and it is keeping that promise. {{promise}} That is the other side of every cache. A copy does not know when the original changes. Something has to tell it, or it has to stop trusting itself after a while. {{copy}} In this lesson you choose how long each answer may be wrong. You replace one copy on demand, and delete one from disk. {{replace}} You name static files after their own content, so they never go stale at all. And you serve an old copy on purpose, when the application is down or busy. {{names}} Last, a race. Two requests in the wrong order put the old price back into the cache, right after you removed it. {{race}}
